gen_risks.description: Insufficient MRV capacity hampers verification of borrowers’ sustainability performance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide technical assistance to develop standardized MRV tools, fund validation services, and train both borrowers and lenders on data collection.
gen_risks.evidence: Limited availability of credible MRV systems constrains lenders’ capacity to evaluate the environmental performance and credit risk of borrowers.

gen_risks.description: High validation and verification costs for SLLs may be passed to borrowers after pilot, reducing uptake.
gen_risks.mitigation: Phase‑in cost sharing, keep a subsidy pool for early borrowers, and negotiate cost‑recovery limits in loan agreements.
gen_risks.evidence: ex‑ante validation and ex‑post verification costs of SLLs … after the piloting stage, this cost is expected to be shifted to the borrowers.

gen_risks.description: Operationalising the new Sustainability‑Linked Loan instrument may encounter implementation challenges.
gen_risks.mitigation: Pilot SLLs with detailed guidelines, engage an independent validation entity, and embed step‑down pricing incentives to encourage compliance.
gen_risks.evidence: particular focus will be given to developing the detailed framework for operationalising this instrument in line with industry standards.

gen_risks.description: Credit risk of beneficiary enterprises could lead to loan defaults affecting NAFIN and PFIs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strengthen credit assessment, use risk‑sharing mechanisms (e.g., guarantees), and monitor loan performance with early‑warning indicators.
gen_risks.evidence: NAFIN will assume the credit risk of the BEs when lending directly and of the PFIs on second‑tier operations.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient private co‑financing (20 % BE, 30 % PFI) may limit project scale.
gen_risks.mitigation: Create incentive packages for private investors, secure anchor‑company commitments early, and track co‑financing targets quarterly.
gen_risks.evidence: minimum 20 % co‑financing from BE … minimum 30 % co‑financing from PFIs and BEs … mobilise US$89 M private capital.

gen_risks.description: Foreign‑exchange risk for USD‑denominated loans could affect borrowers and NAFIN.
gen_risks.mitigation: Limit USD exposure, provide FX hedging support via swaps, and require natural‑hedge justification in loan eligibility criteria.
gen_risks.evidence: NAFIN will manage the FX risk on its own balance sheet using Mexico’s well‑developed currency swap market.

gen_risks.description: Delay in adopting the Project Operations Manual may postpone implementation activities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set clear milestones for POM finalisation, conduct interim reviews, and allocate dedicated staff to fast‑track approval.
gen_risks.evidence: The Borrower shall adopt the Project Operations Manual in form and substance satisfactory to the Bank.

gen_risks.description: Procurement capacity gaps at NAFIN could cause delays or non‑compliance with WB rules.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint a qualified procurement professional, provide hands‑on training from the Bank, and implement a monitoring checklist for each procurement.
gen_risks.evidence: NAFIN’s experience has mainly focused on overseeing… not directly involved… NAFIN will appoint an internal procurement professional… Bank will provide hands‑on training.

gen_risks.description: Low uptake by SMEs due to limited technical capacity and high transaction costs.
gen_risks.mitigation: Run targeted outreach, simplify application procedures, subsidise MRV costs, and provide bundled TA to reduce transaction burdens.
gen_risks.evidence: SMEs lack adequate access to the loan products … high MRV costs and limited capacity to structure, appraise and monitor investments.

gen_risks.description: Gender gap may limit participation of women‑led firms, affecting inclusive outcomes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Introduce gender‑inclusive eligibility criteria, conduct dedicated outreach to women‑owned firms, and offer gender‑focused capacity‑building workshops.
gen_risks.evidence: Women‑owned/led firms have lower access to formal financing… only 42 % have accessed credit… Project will address gender gap by channeling financing to women‑inclusive enterprises.

gen_risks.description: Changes in Sustainable Taxonomy or related regulations could affect eligibility of loans.
gen_risks.mitigation: Maintain continuous dialogue with the Ministry of Finance, embed flexibility clauses in the POM, and monitor regulatory updates closely.
gen_risks.evidence: Mexico has launched a Sustainable Taxonomy and a Sustainable Financing Mobilisation Strategy… market for sustainable finance instruments remains nascent.

gen_risks.description: Climate‑related physical risks (extreme weather) may impair beneficiary firms’ operations and loan repayment.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate climate‑risk assessments into loan underwriting, promote resilience‑enhancing investments, and explore insurance or risk‑pooling mechanisms.
gen_risks.evidence: Mexico is highly vulnerable to climate change… translate into increased operational costs, reduced productivity, and heightened financial distress for SMEs and mid‑caps.

gen_risks.description: Limited market acceptance of SLL/GL instruments could reduce demand for financing.
gen_risks.mitigation: Leverage anchor‑company commitments, showcase pilot successes, and develop demand‑generation campaigns with industry associations.
gen_risks.evidence: the market for sustainable finance instruments remains nascent and concentrated among large corporations.

gen_risks.description: Potential fraud or corruption in loan disbursement and monitoring.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement strict anti‑corruption controls, independent audits, and a robust grievance redress mechanism as required by the loan agreement.
gen_risks.evidence: arrangements for preventing, detecting, reporting, investigation, remediation … compliance with the Anti‑Corruption Guidelines.

gen_risks.description: PFIs have limited experience offering green or sustainable loans, affecting loan quality and monitoring.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide dedicated TA to PFIs, develop standard appraisal templates, and set up a PFI‑specific MRV support unit.
gen_risks.evidence: less than 15 % of Mexican banks offer dedicated green or sustainable loan products; green lending represents less than 1 % of their loan books.

gt_risks.description: The Project channels financing to SMEs/mid-caps via NAFIN through Green Loans (GLs) and Sustainability-Linked Loans (SLLs). For GLs, E&S risk is limited (resources go to a pre-screened positive list), but SLLs operate as corporate loans, making site-specific impacts harder to trace and creating risk around traceability of environmental outcomes and possible greenwashing if sustainability targets are weak or under-monitored.
gt_risks.mitigation: NAFIN prepared an Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS) summary covering main E&S risks by key sector, disclosed at appraisal.

gt_risks.description: Introduction of new financial instruments (notably SLLs) not currently deployed in Mexico, which may lack sufficient demand, drives the technical design risk rating.
gt_risks.mitigation: Substantial TA to NAFIN, PFIs, and beneficiary enterprises (BEs) to support instrument design/deployment; GFPP grant to advance instrument design during preparation; NAFIN required to prepare and adopt a Sustainable Finance Framework (covering SLLs and GLs) acceptable to the Bank prior to effectiveness; draw on global best practices from comparable SLL facilities; Bank hands-on support during initial deployment.

gt_risks.description: The Project requires close coordination and participation of several stakeholders: different units within NAFIN, participating financial institutions (PFIs), beneficiary enterprises, and large anchor companies heading the green value chains (GVCs).
gt_risks.mitigation: Develop and deploy engagement/communication strategies pre-implementation via GFPP plus ongoing TA; establish a dedicated project implementation team within NAFIN with clear roles/responsibilities; formalize PFI participation through legal agreements defining reporting obligations and performance expectations; proactive NAFIN/WB engagement with anchor companies to encourage supplier-firm participation.

gt_risks.description: Risk that SMEs, mid-caps, and participating financial institutions may not take up the new SLL/GL products at the expected pace or scale, given evolving global sustainability policies, limited familiarity with the instruments, and possible overestimation of market demand.
gt_risks.mitigation: NAFIN business-development efforts for sustainable finance; targeted awareness and capacity-building for potential borrowers; TA to help beneficiary enterprises prepare Sustainability Plans and green investment proposals; monitor product uptake with scope to adjust instrument design/eligibility criteria, subject to Bank approval.
